items.title: Anup Bagchi takes charge as HDFC Bank MD & CEO
HDFC Bank appoints Anup Bagchi as MD & CEO effective Oct 27, 2026
Anup Bagchi takes charge as HDFC Bank CEO and MD, succeeds Jagdishan
items.summary:
Country's largest private sector lender HDFC Bank on  Tuesday said that Anup Bagchi has taken charge as its managing director and chief executive.
His predecessor, Sashidhar Jagdishan, vacated office on Monday after the completion of his term, the bank informed exchanges.
Bagchi, an ICICI Group veteran, is the first outsider to head HDFC Bank in its over-three-decade history. His previous assignment was as the MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance.
He joins HDFC Bank at a time when the lender is battling a slew of challenges, including ones on core income growth and margins, which have made investors wary.
In brief comments on an earnings call which he attended, Bagchi said a part of the work on the bank's 2023 merger with housing finance major parent HDFC is yet to be executed and also announced that he will be meeting all the stakeholders to better understand the bank.

Top 10 firms lose ₹1.55  trillion in mcap as HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finance fall
items.summary:
The combined market valuation of eight of the top 10 most valuable firms fell by Rs 1.55 lakh crore last week, with HDFC Bank and Bajaj Finance accounting for most of the losses.
In a holiday-truncated week, the 30-share BSE Sensex tumbled 1,605.44 points, or 2.15 per cent, while the 50-share NSE Nifty slumped 546.15 points, or 2.36 per cent.
Tracking the weak trend in equities, the total market capitalisation of BSE-listed firms fell by Rs 20,78,774.28 crore over four sessions to Rs 4,51,83,393.14 crore from Rs 4,72,62,167.42 crore recorded on October 16.
Among the top 10 listed companies, eight lost Rs 1,55,671.9 crore, while two, Tata Consultancy Services and Larsen & Toubro, closed the week with valuation gains.
Among major losers, the market valuation of HDFC Bank tumbled Rs 55,506.95 crore to Rs 10,67,121.12 crore. The company's stock fell 5 per cent during the last week.
Bajaj Finance's valuation eroded by Rs 34,180.51 crore to Rs 5,77,146.21 crore.

Coforge Q2 Net Profit Jumps 56.5% to ₹588 Crore on AI-Led Deal Execution
Coforge Q2 results: Net profit surges 56.5% to ₹588 cr, revenue up 53.6%
items.summary:
Coforge posted a 56.5 per cent increase in consolidated profit to Rs 588 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by AI-led execution of deals, the company said on Friday.
The IT firm had posted a net profit of Rs 375.8 crore in the same period a year ago.
"Right now the margin uptake that we are seeing is in the existing fixed price projects where AI is getting infused," Coforge Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Sudhir Singh, said during the company's earnings call.
Coforge signed 8 large deals the highest number signed in a single quarter  across North America, Europe and Australia, which led to a total contract value of the new orders of USD 1.04 billion during the reported quarter.
The company increased the operational profit margin guidance to 17 per cent for the next year from the range of 15.5 per cent to 16 per cent.
Revenue from operations during the reported quarter increased by 53.6 per cent to Rs 6,171 crore from Rs 4,016 crore a year
